verified.note: Supplemental Material S4 of arXiv:2407.20629 (identical in the PRL supplement) | 8x8x3 = 192-site periodic kagome torus, H = J sum S_i.S_j (Eq. 1), energy per site | Printed unsigned ("E = 0.42868 ± 0.00003 (E = 0.42724 ± 0.00003) for P-A (periodic-periodic (P-P)) BC"); the sign is the paper's own: its Fig. S7 plots the same quantity on an axis from -0.4280 to -0.4290, and it quotes Ran et al.'s -0.42866(2) as 0.42866(2). P-A and P-P are boundary conditions on the spinon mean-field state; the spin torus is periodic in both, as in VarBench's own baseline for this cluster. The paper does not say how the degenerate Dirac-point level is filled under P-P.

compute.reported_as: In Ref. [8], the variational energy per site E = 0.42866(2) for the lattice size 8 x 8 x 3 with the periodic-antiperiodic (P-A) boundary condition (BC). And our calculation indicates E = 0.42868 +/- 0.00003 (E = 0.42724 +/- 0.00003) for P-A (periodic-periodic (P-P)) BC with 4 x 10^5 samples for the averages, one sample after 240 update with sufficient statistical independent.
compute.source: Supplemental Material Sec. S4 Finite-size effect, arXiv:2407.20629 (compute pass 2026-09-16)
compute.note: Statement covers both the P-A and P-P 8x8x3 DSL energies: 4 x 10^5 Monte Carlo samples, one sample every 240 updates. The DSL trial state here has nearest-neighbour hopping with fixed [0, pi] flux and no Jastrow, so it is essentially parameter-free, but the paper does not state a parameter count for it (it states "15 variational parameters" only for the Z3 QSL ansatz); parameters left null. No hardware, core-hours or wall-clock stated anywhere in the main text or supplement.

compute.reported_as: Abstract: Furthermore, even without variational parameters, the energy turns out to be very close to that found by exact diagonalization. || Main text: For spin-1/2 nearest neighbor anti-ferromagnetic Heisenberg model Eq.(1), we did the Monte Carlo calculation for energies of projected spin liquid states on lattices with 8x8 and 12x12 unit cells (each unit cell has 3 sites). We choose mixed boundary conditions; i.e., periodic along one Bravais lattice vector, and anti-periodic along the other Bravais lattice vector. The results are summarized in Table I. [...] It is striking that even though the projected U(1)-Dirac state has no variational parameter, it has an energy which is even lower than some numerical estimates of ground state energy. [...] It turns out that the calculation of energy <Psi_prj|H|Psi_prj> can be implemented by a Monte Carlo approach with power law complexity, which means that one can do a fairly large lattice.[12]
compute.source: Abstract; main text (Monte Carlo study paragraph and discussion of Table I/II); Table I, arXiv:cond-mat/0611414 (compute pass 2026-09-16)
compute.note: parameters = 0 is verbatim: the projected U(1)-Dirac spin liquid SL-[0,pi] 'has no variational parameter' (the mean-field hopping pattern is fixed; the Gutzwiller projection is exact). No sample count, Monte Carlo sweeps, hardware or run time stated anywhere in the paper (statistical error 2e-5 per site in Table I only). Energy = -0.42866(2) per site (8x8x3 lattice, mixed boundary conditions) in the worklist's units. Source file: sources/cond-mat-0611414.txt.
